## Claims
- [source-backed] \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) has the integral Schur basis indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\), and truncated Littlewood–Richardson multiplication. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218; 263-269]
- [source-backed] The involution \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 481-485]
- [computed] For \([222,4^5]\subset\Lambda/I_{5,4}\) and its conjugate \([33,5^4]\subset\Lambda/I_{4,5}\), complete Pieri relation lattices and quotient Smith data agree in weights \(6,\ldots,20\): ranks \((1,1,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0)\) and no torsion factors. [artifact 5b6e59b74af1b386568e8d3014cdef276ec80f89225cf5ba2367c73fa3b0a993]
- [proved] Under the accepted quotient-conjugation and ideal-correspondence premises, partition conjugation induces an integral graded isomorphism
  \[
  J_v/A_+J_v\cong J_{v^\vee}/A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee}.
  \]
  Consequently it preserves each degree’s torsion subgroup, invariant factors, and free rank.

## Strategy
Put \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(A^\vee=\Lambda/I_{q,r}\), \(q=n-r\), and let
\[
\Omega(\bar s_\lambda)=\bar s_{\lambda'}.
\]
The accepted premises give \(\Omega:A\!\xrightarrow{\sim}\!A^\vee\) and \(\Omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee}\). Since \(|\lambda'|=|\lambda|\), \(\Omega\) is graded; hence \(\Omega(A_+)=A^\vee_+\).

For every degree \(d\),
\[
\Omega((A_+J_v)_d)
=\Omega\!\left(\sum_{e>0}A_eJ_{v,d-e}\right)
=\sum_{e>0}A^\vee_eJ_{v^\vee,d-e}
=(A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee})_d.
\]
Thus \(\Omega\) descends degreewise to the displayed quotient isomorphism. An integral abelian-group isomorphism preserves torsion subgroups and free ranks degreewise.

Requested target: established. The right-hand \(A_+\) in the requested notation is \(A^\vee_+\).

## Gaps
The finite artifact checks only its stated non-self-conjugate inputs and is not used to prove the universal statement.
